title: President Obama's Health Care Plan: Soup to Nuts
summary: Part two of a four-part healthcare reform series. Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant, joined by Molly Edmonds, lay out the health care proposals in play in 2009 without political commentary: Obama's eight principles, the House and Senate bills (including the Senate Finance Committee bill still pending), the individual and employer mandates and their penalties, Medicaid expansion, subsidies on a sliding scale, the insurance marketplace with plain-language plan comparisons and minimum benefits, the proposed public option, pre-existing condition protections, out-of-pocket caps, Medicare Advantage cuts, bundled payments and comparative effectiveness panels, and funding options such as taxing high-income people, the employer health insurance tax exclusion, and taxing high-end plans. Parts three and four are promised to cover criticisms and myths versus truths.

segments.title: Introduction and series overview
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode with guest Molly Edmonds and explain that this is part two of a four-part healthcare series, with no politics discussed in this part.

segments.title: Obama's proposal and the eight principles
segments.summary: The hosts explain that Obama laid out eight principles and Congress drafted the bills, noting the Clinton-era plan that failed, the House bill HR 3200, and the pending Senate Finance Committee bill. They list the principles, including affordable coverage, pre-existing conditions, prevention, job change coverage, quality and safety, choice of doctors, protection from bankruptcy, and reducing long-term cost growth.

segments.title: Individual and employer mandates and subsidies
segments.summary: The hosts describe the individual mandate to carry health insurance, with a Senate penalty of seven hundred fifty dollars a year and a House penalty of up to 2.5 percent of adjusted income, and an employer mandate. They discuss Medicaid expansion and sliding-scale subsidies based on the federal poverty level.

segments.title: Insurance marketplace, plain language, and minimum benefits
segments.summary: The hosts explain the proposed insurance marketplace modeled on the way members of Congress choose plans, with plain-language disclosure and minimum required benefits. They mention the Massachusetts experiment, grandfathered plans, and the small business exemption from the employer mandate.

segments.title: Public option
segments.summary: The hosts describe the proposed government-run public health insurance option, how it would have to fund itself through premiums rather than federal injections, that its details were still unsettled, and that a co-op alternative was floated. They note the limits on keeping employer-based coverage.

segments.title: Insurer rules: pre-existing conditions and spending caps
segments.summary: The hosts explain proposed bans on discrimination based on pre-existing conditions, the end of lifetime spending caps, and a cap on annual out-of-pocket consumer costs to reduce medical bankruptcies.

segments.title: Medicare and Medicaid waste, bundling, and treatment effectiveness
segments.summary: The hosts discuss cutting waste in Medicare and Medicaid, the roughly 170 billion dollar a year Medicare Advantage overpayment, bundled payments for care, and a panel reviewing which treatments work best, with doctors still able to choose other treatments.

segments.title: Paying for reform: taxes and funding options
segments.summary: The hosts review funding ideas including taxing people earning above a threshold, eliminating the employer health insurance tax exclusion, taxing high-end insurance plans, and a trillion-dollar ten-year cost estimate with two-thirds said to be covered by waste cuts.

segments.title: Wrap-up and tease for part three
segments.summary: The hosts thank Molly Edmonds and preview part three on criticisms and part four on myths and truths, then close with sponsor and network sign-off.
